// why: `packages/core/tsconfig.json` includes `src` only, so NOTHING under `test/` is typechecked by
the package build (proven by planting `const x: number = "a string"` in a test file and
watching the typecheck exit 0). A compile-time guard that no compiler runs is not a guard,
and the rule evaluator's input contract depends on exactly one: `auth` is
REQUIRED on `EvaluateRulesInput` and unread by the evaluator, so a runtime assertion cannot
see it and the only thing that can enforce it is tsc.
This project compiles `test/contract/` — type-level assertions, no runtime behaviour — and the
root tsconfig references it, so `pnpm typecheck` builds it on every push.
`test/rules-contract.test.ts` invokes the same build so the suite reports the same failure
under a test name. Modelled on `packages/api/tsconfig.contract.json`.
Deliberately NOT the whole `test/` tree: this project must fail for one reason only.
